title: Crestline Fleet Account Safety Work Allowance on Disputed Over-Limit Tickets
content:
On a Crestline Fleet Account, for a ticket a business disputes as an unapproved over-limit ticket, a safety allowance is added to the authorized amount, because Crestline's fleet programs let a driver authorize safety work alone when a vehicle cannot safely wait.

## Safety allowance

| What the ticket includes | Safety allowance |
|---|---|
| tire or brake work | 100.00 |
| battery work but no tire or brake work | 50.00 |
| none of these | nothing |

A ticket includes a kind of work when, among the vehicle's invoices dated the same day as the disputed invoice from the same store, at least one is in that service category (tires, brakes or battery).

## Combinations

| Tires or brakes invoice that day from that store | Battery invoice that day from that store | Safety allowance |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 100.00 |
| yes | no | 100.00 |
| no | yes | 50.00 |
| no | no | 0.00 |

The allowance is one figure per ticket: a ticket with both tires and brakes invoices still carries 100.00, not 100.00 for each.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

On an account whose authorized amount would otherwise be 640.00, a disputed battery-only ticket raises it by the 50.00 safety allowance, to 690.00. Had the ticket included a brakes invoice, the allowance would be 100.00.
